lines: The Testament dative & Inventar of
the guidis geir debtis & sowmes of money qlkis
pertenit to umqle Johne glasgow sailler in Saltcoittis
within the parochin of Ardrossane
[who] deceissit in the moneth of December [1636]
faithfullie maid & gevin up be Issobell gray his relict
In name & behalff of Kathrein & Agnes glasgow
his lawfull bairnes [and executors dative wording partly unresolved]
to the defunct thair father be the decreit of the
Commissaris of glasgow [day unresolved] Aprile 1637 zeiris
Inventar
[faded inventory and inward/outward debt entries unresolved]
[confirmation formula at foot partly unresolved]
The qlk day [compeirit] personallie Johne Broune
sailler in Saltcoittis And of his awin consent
actit him self as cautioun [administrative continuation unresolved]
Kathrein & Agnes glasgow lawfull bairnes of
umqle Johne glasgow sailler in Saltcoittis
[obligation and closing formula unresolved]
[following Muir estate excluded]

plain_english: John Glasgow was a sailor in Saltcoats within Ardrossan parish and died in December 1636.

Isobell Gray is expressly his relict or widow. Katherine and Agnes Glasgow are expressly his lawful children, and the deceased is called their father. Their executor role is additional administration, not the basis for the relationship.
John Broune, another sailor in Saltcoats, acted as cautioner. The record gives no kin term for him.
The record does not state that Isobell was the children's mother and does not name Mary as a child.
The household remains distinct from Glasgow-1030 and Jonet Mathie: no bridge in this testament connects them.
findings: Confirmed: testament dative, sailor occupation, Saltcoats, Ardrossan parish and December 1636 death month.
Confirmed: Isobell Gray is John's relict; maternity of Katherine and Agnes is not stated.
Confirmed: Kathrein and Agnes Glasgow are lawful children and John is expressly their father.
Confirmed: the caution repeats the daughters and their father's Saltcoats occupation/locality.
Confirmed: John Broune is a Saltcoats sailor and cautioner; no kinship follows.
Excluded: Glasgow-1030 is not identified as this sailor, and Glasgow-3539/Mary is not established as his daughter.
changes_from_previous: Old: widow, daughters and cautioner readings were maintained. New: each is confirmed unchanged after rereading the full clauses and continuation.
Old: Glasgow-1030 was excluded as the present identification. New: exclusion is confirmed; no new bridge appears in the accounts or caution.
Old: no Mary was established. New: confirmed unchanged after checking all three pages.
No walkthrough text or geometry changed because the family and exclusion conclusions remain unchanged.
unresolved: Whether Isobell Gray was the mother of Katherine and Agnes.
Existing-profile identities for John, Isobell, Katherine, Agnes and John Broune.
The index confirms the court date as 11 April 1637; manuscript inventory descriptions, debt parties and full confirmation/caution wording remain unresolved.
Any connection to Glasgow-1030 requires an external documentary bridge.
profiles: John Glasgow: excluded as the present Saltcoats identification
Mary Glasgow: not established as this sailor's daughter
confidence_statement: High for John, occupation/locality, Isobell as relict, Katherine and Agnes as lawful children, and John Broune as cautioner. High that the testament supplies no bridge to Glasgow-1030. Low for faded account parties and precise administrative day.
